newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indonesia wants to prepay high cost ADB loans.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia wants to prepay high cost ADB loans.

text.p: Indonesia wants to prepay expensive loans from the Asian Development Bank by using funds earned from privatisation, finance minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Monday.

Addressing fellow ADB governors on the second day of the bank's three-day annual meeting, Muhammad said Indonesia's strong economic growth had enabled repayment and in some cases advance repayment of foreign loans.

"The government of Indonesia is firmly committed to fully honouring all of its international financial obligations. Indeed, the government will continue to prepay the high-cost loans from the Asian Development Bank by utilising the proceeds of funds raised by our ongoing privatisation programmes and budget surpluses," he said.
The ADB, which is marking 30 years in existence in Japan where it was formed, gives loans at commercial rates of interest from its ordinary capital resources.
The bank is known more, however, for the virtually interest-free loans it provides from an aid window called the Asian Development Fund (ADF).
In addition to loans taken at commercial rates, Indonesia has also received loans from the ADF, but with its improving economic situation it is now depending less on the fund.
Indonesia has, in fact, begun contributing to the fund.
"While Indonesia remains an ADF borrower, it has also agreed to support this effort by making a financial contribution to the ADF," the finance minister said.
